guard: The manager hosts workflow runs (SPEC 14.3): run-start refuses an invalid program with the language's records and answers only once the run is recorded; a checkpoint parked in the hosted drive is answered from outside; a manager restart takes a run recorded running back under the next epoch.
why: The suite runs the manager from its built package, so a mutation on manager src is seen through
that build and afterRestore rebuilds so the restored source is the artifact again. Each mutant
aims at one guarantee the family makes: validation before any record, the answer-after-record
wait, and the boot reconcile filter that decides which runs a successor takes back.

mutations.name: run-start skips validation
mutations.expectRed: run-start refuses an invalid program as bad-request
mutations.cell: run-start refuses an invalid program as bad-request
mutations.note: Keeps `verdict` narrowed inside the block: a bare `&& false` fails tsc (the block reads `verdict.errors`) and grades WRONG-RED about the build, not the guard.

mutations.name: run-start answers before the record lands
mutations.expectRed: the run's record exists by the time run-start has answered
mutations.cell: the run's record exists by the time run-start has answered

mutations.name: the boot reconcile takes back every run except the running ones
mutations.expectRed: the successor takes the parked run back
mutations.cell: the successor takes the parked run back: still running, now under epoch 2, the pause still open
mutations.note: The flipped filter keeps `status` narrowed for the rows below (an `|| true` narrows it to never and fails tsc). It resumes the completed runs, which replay to completion again, and leaves the parked one at epoch 1, which the takeback cell reads.
